questions.q: Your company buys 200 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses but nobody can use Copilot in Word yet. What is the most likely reason?
options: Copilot licenses activate automatically 30 days after purchase
The licenses were purchased but not assigned to individual users or to a group
A conditional access policy is blocking Word
Copilot needs to be installed from the Microsoft Store on each PC
questions.explain: Buying a licence and assigning it are two separate steps. A licence sitting in your tenant does nothing until it is attached to a user account (directly, or through group-based licensing). Once assigned, the Copilot features light up in the apps.

wrong.0: Nothing activates on its own; an admin has to assign the licence.
wrong.2: Conditional access controls sign-in, not whether a Copilot feature appears.
wrong.3: Copilot is built into the Microsoft 365 apps the user already has - there is nothing to install from a store.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of group-based licensing in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: It makes licences cheaper per user
It removes the need to buy licences for guest users
It lets one licence be shared by several users at once
Licences are assigned and removed automatically as people join or leave the group
questions.explain: With group-based licensing you assign the licence to a group instead of to people. Anyone added to that group gets the licence automatically, and anyone removed loses it - which is why it scales so much better than clicking through users one at a time.

wrong.0: The price per licence is unchanged; only the assignment method differs.
wrong.1: Guests still need appropriate licensing for licensed features.
wrong.2: A licence is still one user, one licence. Sharing is not allowed.

questions.q: Where would an administrator go to add and verify a custom domain name such as contoso.com for the tenant?
options: Exchange admin center > Mail flow
Microsoft Purview portal > Data map
Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Domains
SharePoint admin center > Settings
questions.explain: Domain names are tenant-level settings, so they live in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Settings > Domains. That is where you add a domain, get the DNS records to prove you own it, and verify it.

wrong.0: Mail flow handles connectors and routing rules for mail already in the tenant, not domain ownership.
wrong.1: Purview is for compliance and data governance.
wrong.3: The SharePoint admin center manages sites and sharing, not tenant domains.

questions.q: An admin needs to change the tenant's organisation profile - the company name, address, and the release preference for new features. Which admin center is used?
options: Teams admin center
Microsoft Entra admin center
Microsoft 365 admin center
Power Platform admin center
questions.explain: Organisation-wide profile and settings, including release preferences (targeted release), live in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Settings > Org settings.

wrong.0: The Teams admin center is scoped to Teams only.
wrong.1: Entra handles identity objects - users, groups, roles, and access policies.
wrong.3: Power Platform manages environments, apps, flows, and Copilot Studio agents.

questions.q: A department wants a single address, sales@contoso.com, that several people can read and send from without paying for an extra licence. What should the admin create in the Exchange admin center?
options: A Microsoft 365 group
A shared mailbox
A distribution group
A dynamic distribution list
questions.explain: A shared mailbox is a mailbox that multiple people open with their own credentials. It has its own address, keeps a common history of sent items, and does not need its own licence under normal storage limits.

wrong.0: This would work but it creates a whole team workspace (mailbox, site, planner); the simplest fit for a shared address is a shared mailbox.
wrong.2: A distribution group just forwards a message to every member's own mailbox - there is no shared copy or shared sent folder.
wrong.3: Same limitation as a distribution group, with membership calculated from user attributes.

questions.q: Which object should an admin create so that one email address delivers a copy of every message to each of 40 employees' own mailboxes?
options: A resource mailbox
A security group
A shared mailbox
A distribution group
questions.explain: A distribution group (distribution list) exists to fan a message out to all its members' personal mailboxes. It is a mail-only object with no storage of its own.

wrong.0: Resource mailboxes represent rooms and equipment for booking.
wrong.1: Security groups grant access to resources; they are not mail-enabled by default.
wrong.2: A shared mailbox holds one common copy that people open, rather than delivering to each person.

questions.q: In SharePoint in Microsoft 365, what is the correct order of containers from largest to smallest?
options: Document library > site > folder > file
Site > folder > document library > file
Site > document library > folder > file
Folder > site > document library > file
questions.explain: A site is the top container. Inside a site you have lists and document libraries, inside a library you can have folders, and files live inside those. Knowing this order matters because permissions flow down the same path.

wrong.0: A library cannot contain a site; it lives inside one.
wrong.1: Folders belong to libraries, so the library comes first.
wrong.3: Folders live inside libraries, not the other way round.

cues: order of containers from largest to smallest

questions.q: Which default SharePoint site permission level allows a user to add and edit documents but not change site settings or permissions?
options: Site Collection Administrator
Full Control (Owners)
Read (Visitors)
Edit (Members)
questions.explain: The default Members group has the Edit permission level: add, edit and delete content in lists and libraries, but no control over site settings or who else has access.

wrong.0: A site collection administrator has the highest level of control over the site.
wrong.1: Full Control is the Owners group - it can change settings and permissions.
wrong.2: Read is view-only; visitors cannot add or edit documents.

cues: add and edit documents but not change site settings or permissions

questions.q: A user needs to view files on a project site but must not be able to change anything. Which group should they be added to?
options: Site collection administrators
Owners
Visitors
Members
questions.explain: Visitors carry Read permission - open and view content, nothing more. It is the standard least-privilege choice for someone who only needs to consume information.

wrong.0: This is the most powerful role on the site - the opposite of what is needed.
wrong.1: Owners can change settings and grant access to others.
wrong.3: Members can edit and delete content.

cues: must not be able to change anything

questions.q: Why does SharePoint permission design matter so much before rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot?
options: Copilot requires every site to be set to Read for everyone
Copilot ignores SharePoint permissions and reads all tenant content
Copilot only works on sites with unique permissions
Copilot can surface any content the signed-in user already has permission to see, so overly broad permissions become visible fast
questions.explain: Copilot inherits the user's existing access - it never shows content a person could not already open. The catch is that content someone technically had access to but never found by browsing can now surface instantly in an answer, which is why loose permissions suddenly become obvious.

wrong.0: That would be the worst possible configuration and is not required.
wrong.1: Copilot strictly honours existing permissions.
wrong.2: Copilot works regardless of whether permissions are inherited or unique.

questions.q: An admin must stop external users from being added to any team in the organisation. Where is this configured?
options: Teams admin center - external access and guest access settings
Microsoft Purview - retention policies
SharePoint admin center - site creation settings
Exchange admin center - mail flow rules
questions.explain: Teams collaboration with people outside the tenant is governed by external access (federation with other domains) and guest access settings in the Teams admin center.

wrong.1: Retention decides how long content is kept, not who can join.
wrong.2: That governs SharePoint site creation, not Teams membership.
wrong.3: Mail flow rules affect email routing only.

cues: external users from being added to any team

questions.q: In Microsoft Teams, what is a channel?
options: A licence type assigned to team members
A type of security group in Entra ID
A separate tenant for a business unit
A dedicated section inside a team for a topic, project or department
questions.explain: A team is the container for a group of people; channels are the subdivisions inside it where conversations and files for a specific topic live. Each standard channel gets its own folder in the team's SharePoint site.

wrong.0: Channels are not licensed objects.
wrong.1: Channels are Teams objects, not directory objects.
wrong.2: Tenants are organisation-wide and unrelated to channels.

questions.q: How does an administrator apply different meeting settings to executives than to the rest of the staff?
options: Assign a custom Teams meeting policy to the executives
Give executives Global Administrator rights
Create a separate tenant for executives
Change the org-wide setting each time an executive schedules a meeting
questions.explain: Teams policies exist precisely for this: you create a policy with the settings you want and assign it to specific users or groups, leaving everyone else on the global (org-wide default) policy.

wrong.1: Admin rights control administration, not meeting behaviour - and this would be a serious security mistake.
wrong.2: A second tenant is a huge, unnecessary change.
wrong.3: Org-wide settings apply to everyone and cannot be changed per meeting.

questions.q: Which three principles form the Zero Trust model?
options: Authenticate once, authorise always, audit yearly
Block external users, allow internal users, log everything
Trust but verify, defend the perimeter, encrypt everything
Verify explicitly, use least privilege access, assume breach
questions.explain: Zero Trust rests on three ideas: verify explicitly (always authenticate and authorise using all available signals), use least privilege access (just enough access, just in time), and assume breach (design as if an attacker is already inside).

wrong.0: Not a Microsoft Zero Trust principle.
wrong.1: An inside/outside distinction is exactly what Zero Trust rejects.
wrong.2: This describes the older perimeter-based model Zero Trust replaced.

questions.q: Under Zero Trust, what does 'assume breach' mean in practice?
options: Report a data breach to regulators every quarter
Assume every user is malicious and block all access
Never allow remote access to company data
Segment access, verify end-to-end encryption, and use analytics to detect threats as if an attacker is already present
questions.explain: 'Assume breach' is a design stance, not an accusation. You limit blast radius through segmentation and least privilege, encrypt in transit and at rest, and monitor continuously - so that if something is compromised the damage stays contained.

wrong.0: Breach reporting is a compliance obligation, not a Zero Trust principle.
wrong.1: Zero Trust verifies people rather than blocking them outright.
wrong.2: Zero Trust is what makes secure remote access possible.

questions.q: A user signs in successfully but gets an 'access denied' message opening a SharePoint site. Which is failing?
options: Multifactor authentication - a second factor was missing
Federation - the identity provider is unreachable
Authorisation - who they are was proven, but they lack permission to that resource
Authentication - their identity could not be verified
questions.explain: Authentication answers 'who are you?' and it clearly succeeded, because the sign-in worked. Authorisation answers 'what are you allowed to do?' - and that is what has denied the site.

wrong.0: A missing second factor blocks the sign-in, not one specific site.
wrong.1: A federation failure would also stop the sign-in entirely.
wrong.3: If authentication had failed, the sign-in itself would not have completed.

questions.q: Which authentication method is considered the most secure of the options listed?
options: SMS text message codes
A FIDO2 security key (phishing-resistant, passwordless)
Voice call verification
A password with a security question
questions.explain: FIDO2 keys are phishing-resistant: the secret never leaves the device and is bound to the real site, so a fake login page gets nothing. Microsoft ranks phishing-resistant passwordless methods at the top of the strength list.

wrong.0: SMS can be intercepted or defeated by SIM swapping - it is the weakest MFA option.
wrong.2: Voice calls have the same interception weaknesses as SMS.
wrong.3: Security questions are easy to research or guess.

questions.q: What does multifactor authentication require a user to provide?
options: Evidence from at least two different categories, such as something they know plus something they have
A password entered twice for confirmation
Approval from two different administrators
Two different passwords
questions.explain: MFA means combining categories: something you know (password/PIN), something you have (phone, security key), or something you are (fingerprint, face). Two items from the same category is not MFA.

wrong.1: Retyping is a typo check, not a security factor.
wrong.2: That describes an approval workflow, not authentication.
wrong.3: Two passwords are both 'something you know' - one stolen credential list defeats both.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a conditional access policy?
options: A firewall rule that blocks IP address ranges at the network edge
A licence that must be purchased for every user in the tenant
A retention rule that decides how long data is kept
An if-then rule that evaluates signals such as user, device, location and risk, then grants, blocks or adds requirements to access
questions.explain: Conditional access is the Zero Trust policy engine in Entra ID. It gathers signals (who, what device, where from, how risky), then makes a decision: allow, block, or allow with conditions such as MFA or a compliant device.

wrong.0: Conditional access works at the identity layer, not the network layer.
wrong.1: It is a feature (requiring Entra ID P1), not a per-action purchase.
wrong.2: That is Purview data lifecycle management.

questions.q: Which of these is a common conditional access grant control?
options: Delete the user account
Create a retention label
Assign a Microsoft 365 licence
Require multifactor authentication
questions.explain: Grant controls are the requirements attached to an allowed sign-in: require MFA, require a compliant or Entra-joined device, require an approved client app, or require terms of use to be accepted.

wrong.0: Conditional access never deletes accounts.
wrong.1: Retention labels belong to Microsoft Purview.
wrong.2: Licensing is separate from access policy.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of single sign-on (SSO)?
options: Passwords are no longer required anywhere in the organisation
Every application gets its own separate password for extra security
Users authenticate once and gain access to multiple applications without signing in again
All users automatically get administrator rights
questions.explain: SSO lets one verified sign-in carry across many apps. That means fewer passwords to remember (so fewer weak or reused ones), fewer helpdesk resets, and one central place to enforce MFA and conditional access.

wrong.0: SSO is not the same as passwordless, although they combine well.
wrong.1: Separate passwords per app is the problem SSO solves - and it encourages reuse.
wrong.3: SSO has nothing to do with privilege levels.

questions.q: An admin wants to grant a set of people access to a SharePoint site, a Teams team and a shared mailbox using one object. Which should be used?
options: A mail-enabled contact
A Microsoft 365 group
A dynamic administrative unit
A distribution group
questions.explain: A Microsoft 365 group is the membership object that ties collaboration services together - it comes with a shared mailbox, a SharePoint site, and it backs a Teams team.

wrong.0: A contact is just an external address in the directory.
wrong.2: Administrative units scope who admins can manage, not resource access.
wrong.3: A distribution group only delivers email to members.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a security group in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: To store retention settings for documents
To create a shared mailbox and calendar for collaboration
To license Microsoft 365 Copilot on a per-message basis
To grant access to resources and apply policies to a collection of users or devices
questions.explain: Security groups are about access: assign permissions, target conditional access policies, and assign licences to everyone in the group at once. They can also contain devices, which Microsoft 365 groups cannot.

wrong.0: Retention lives in Purview policies, not groups.
wrong.1: That is a Microsoft 365 group.
wrong.2: Billing policies and licences handle that.

questions.q: Several users report they cannot sign in this morning. Which tool shows the specific failure reason and error code for each attempt?
options: SharePoint data access governance reports
Microsoft Purview Content search
The Teams usage report
Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
questions.explain: Entra sign-in logs record every authentication attempt with the status, failure code, the conditional access policies that applied, the device, the location and the app - which is exactly what you need to tell an MFA problem from a blocked policy.

wrong.0: That reports on SharePoint sharing exposure.
wrong.1: Content search finds files and emails for investigations.
wrong.2: Usage reports show adoption numbers, not authentication failures.

cues: specific failure reason and error code

questions.q: Before enabling a new conditional access policy, an admin wants to see who it would affect without actually enforcing it. What should they use?
options: The What If tool in conditional access, or set the policy to report-only mode
Delete the existing policies first
Turn on security defaults
Assign the policy to Global Administrators only
questions.explain: Report-only mode evaluates the policy against real sign-ins and logs what would have happened without blocking anyone. The What If tool simulates a specific user and scenario. Both let you find surprises before users do.

wrong.1: Deleting policies removes protection and tells you nothing.
wrong.2: Security defaults are a basic baseline and conflict with custom conditional access policies.
wrong.3: Testing on your most privileged accounts risks locking yourself out.

questions.q: Which capability flags sign-ins from anonymous IP addresses, unfamiliar locations or impossible travel?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk detections
Microsoft 365 Archive
SharePoint restricted access control
Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
questions.explain: Entra ID Protection scores each sign-in and each user for risk using Microsoft's threat signals - impossible travel, anonymous IPs, leaked credentials and more. Those risk levels can then be used as a condition in conditional access.

wrong.1: Archive moves inactive sites to cheaper storage.
wrong.2: That restricts who can open a SharePoint site.
wrong.3: DLP watches sensitive data leaving, not sign-in behaviour.

cues: anonymous IP addresses, unfamiliar locations or impossible travel

questions.q: How should an administrator interpret the Identity Secure Score in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: As a guarantee that the tenant cannot be breached
As a percentage score with recommended actions that show how closely the tenant follows identity security best practice
As the number of users who have signed in this month
As a measure of how much Copilot is being used
questions.explain: Identity Secure Score compares your configuration against Microsoft's recommended identity practices and gives you a percentage plus a prioritised list of improvement actions. Higher is better, but it is guidance, not a guarantee.

wrong.0: No score can guarantee security.
wrong.2: That is a usage metric, not a security posture score.
wrong.3: Copilot adoption is measured in Copilot Analytics and admin center reports.

questions.q: An investigator needs to know which administrator changed a sharing setting three weeks ago. Where should they look?
options: The Microsoft 365 message center
The SharePoint recycle bin
The unified audit log, searched from Microsoft Purview
The Entra ID Identity Secure Score
questions.explain: The unified audit log records user and admin activity across Microsoft 365 workloads and is searched from Microsoft Purview (Audit). You can filter by date range, activity and user to find exactly who did what.

wrong.0: The message center announces upcoming service changes.
wrong.1: The recycle bin holds deleted items, not a record of setting changes.
wrong.3: Secure Score rates configuration; it does not log individual actions.

cues: which administrator changed a sharing setting three weeks ago

questions.q: What problem does Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) solve?
options: It replaces multifactor authentication for admins
It backs up privileged users' mailboxes
It automatically assigns Microsoft 365 Copilot licences
It removes standing administrative access by making roles eligible and activated just in time, with approval and time limits
questions.explain: With PIM, admins are eligible for a role rather than permanently holding it. They activate it when needed, optionally with justification, approval and MFA, and it expires automatically - so a compromised account is usually not an admin account at that moment.

wrong.0: PIM works alongside MFA and can require it at activation.
wrong.1: PIM does not perform backups.
wrong.2: Licensing is unrelated to PIM.

questions.q: In PIM, what is the difference between an eligible assignment and an active assignment?
options: There is no functional difference
Eligible applies to guests; active applies to employees
Eligible means read-only; active means read-write
Eligible means the user must activate the role when needed; active means they hold its permissions already
questions.explain: An eligible assignment is permission-on-demand: the user has to go and activate it, which creates an audit trail and a time limit. An active assignment is standing access that works right now - which is what PIM aims to minimise.

wrong.0: The difference is the core of how PIM works.
wrong.1: PIM does not distinguish guests from employees this way.
wrong.2: Both can carry the same permissions; the difference is when they apply.

questions.q: What is the difference between an app registration and an enterprise application in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: They are two names for the same object
An app registration defines the application itself; the enterprise application is the instance of it in your tenant, where you control consent, assignment and SSO
App registrations are free; enterprise applications require a licence per app
App registrations are for Microsoft apps; enterprise applications are for third-party apps
questions.explain: Registering an app creates its definition - identity, permissions it can request, redirect URIs. The enterprise application (the service principal) is that app's presence in your tenant, and it is where you decide who can use it, what it has been granted consent for, and how sign-in works.

wrong.0: They are related but distinct objects with different admin purposes.
wrong.2: Neither is licensed per app in that way.
wrong.3: Either kind of app can appear as either object.

questions.q: Which Microsoft Defender XDR service is designed to protect against malicious links and attachments in email and Teams messages?
options: Microsoft Defender for Identity
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Defender for Office 365
questions.explain: Defender for Office 365 covers the collaboration surface - email, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive - with Safe Links, Safe Attachments, anti-phishing policies and automated investigation.

wrong.0: Defender for Identity watches on-premises Active Directory signals for identity attacks.
wrong.1: Defender for Endpoint protects devices such as laptops and servers.
wrong.2: Defender for Cloud Apps discovers and governs the SaaS apps in use.

questions.q: What does the 'XDR' in Microsoft Defender XDR refer to?
options: External domain restriction for guest access
Exchange data recovery
Extra data retention for compliance
Extended detection and response - correlating signals across identities, endpoints, email, apps and data into a single incident
questions.explain: XDR means extended detection and response. Rather than a separate alert per product, Defender XDR stitches related signals across identity, endpoint, email, apps and data into one incident so you see the whole attack story.

wrong.0: Not a real product term.
wrong.1: Not what XDR stands for.
wrong.2: Retention is a Purview concept.

questions.q: Which Microsoft Purview solution classifies and protects content by applying labels that can enforce encryption and visual markings?
options: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
Microsoft Purview Information Protection (sensitivity labels)
Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management
questions.explain: Information Protection is the labelling engine. A sensitivity label travels with the file or email and can apply encryption, watermarks, headers and footers, and access restrictions that persist wherever the content goes.

wrong.0: Communication Compliance scans messages for policy violations such as harassment.
wrong.1: Insider Risk Management detects risky user behaviour patterns.
wrong.3: Data Lifecycle Management decides how long content is kept or when it is deleted.

questions.q: What happens when a document carrying an encrypting sensitivity label is referenced by Microsoft 365 Copilot?
options: Copilot deletes the labelled file
Copilot honours the label's usage rights, and content it generates from that file can inherit the label
Copilot strips the label so the content can be summarised
Copilot ignores labels entirely
questions.explain: Copilot respects the rights a sensitivity label grants. If the user does not have the right to view the content, Copilot will not use it - and when Copilot creates something new from labelled material, the most restrictive label is inherited so the protection carries forward.

wrong.0: Copilot does not delete content.
wrong.2: Labels are never stripped by Copilot.
wrong.3: Honouring labels is one of Copilot's core protections.

questions.q: Which is a valid use case for a sensitivity label?
options: Deciding which users receive a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence
Archiving a SharePoint site that has had no activity for a year
Blocking a user's sign-in from an unfamiliar country
Automatically encrypting any document containing credit card numbers and marking it Confidential
questions.explain: Sensitivity labels classify content and apply protection - encryption, watermarks, restricted sharing - and they can be applied automatically when a sensitive information type such as a credit card number is detected.

wrong.0: Licensing is done in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
wrong.1: That is site lifecycle management / Microsoft 365 Archive.
wrong.2: That is conditional access with Entra ID Protection.

questions.q: What does a Microsoft Purview DLP policy do?
options: Replaces the need for sensitivity labels
Detects sensitive information in content or actions and blocks, warns or audits when it is about to be shared inappropriately
Permanently deletes any file containing sensitive data
Encrypts the entire tenant's storage
questions.explain: DLP watches content in motion - email, Teams messages, SharePoint, OneDrive, endpoints and now AI prompts - and enforces an action when a rule matches: block, block with override, warn the user with a policy tip, or just audit.

wrong.0: DLP and labels complement each other - labels can even be a DLP condition.
wrong.2: DLP does not delete content; it restricts the action.
wrong.3: Encryption at rest is a platform feature, not a DLP action.

questions.q: An employee pastes customer national ID numbers into a Copilot prompt. Which Purview capability can stop that content from being processed?
options: A retention policy
Identity Secure Score
A Teams messaging policy
A DLP policy scoped to AI prompts, which can be created from DSPM for AI
questions.explain: DLP can now be applied to what users type into AI apps. DSPM for AI offers a one-click policy that blocks sensitive information from being submitted in prompts to Copilot and other AI experiences.

wrong.0: Retention controls how long data is kept, not what is typed.
wrong.1: Secure Score rates identity configuration.
wrong.2: Teams messaging policies control chat features such as editing messages.

questions.q: Where does an administrator review and triage alerts generated by DLP policies?
options: The SharePoint recycle bin
The DLP alerts page in the Microsoft Purview portal
The Microsoft 365 message center
Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
questions.explain: DLP alerts appear in the Purview portal under Data loss prevention > Alerts, where you can see the matched policy, the sensitive information found, the user and the action taken, and then set a status such as investigating or resolved.

wrong.0: The recycle bin holds deleted items.
wrong.2: The message center announces service changes.
wrong.3: Sign-in logs cover authentication, not data movement.

questions.q: Which Microsoft Purview solution detects patterns such as an employee downloading unusual volumes of files shortly after resigning?
options: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Microsoft Purview eDiscovery
Microsoft Entra PIM
questions.explain: Insider Risk Management correlates signals - departing employee indicators from HR, mass downloads, renaming files, copying to USB - into risk alerts about people rather than single events, with built-in policy templates like data theft by departing users.

wrong.1: Defender for Endpoint focuses on malware and device threats.
wrong.2: eDiscovery collects content for legal cases.
wrong.3: PIM manages just-in-time admin roles.

questions.q: Why does Insider Risk Management use pseudonymisation by default?
options: To make the alerts run faster
Because Microsoft cannot read customer data
To reduce the tenant's storage costs
To protect user privacy during investigation by hiding usernames until an authorised reviewer needs them
questions.explain: Insider risk work is sensitive by nature, so by default analysts see anonymised identifiers instead of names. That keeps the investigation focused on behaviour and limits who can see who is being reviewed.

wrong.0: Performance is unrelated.
wrong.1: This is a customer privacy control, not a Microsoft access limitation.
wrong.2: Pseudonymisation has no storage effect.

questions.q: Which solution detects inappropriate, harassing or regulatory-sensitive language in Teams chats and email?
options: SharePoint Advanced Management
Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance
Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management
Microsoft Entra ID Protection
questions.explain: Communication Compliance scans messages against policies - offensive language, threats, sensitive information, regulatory phrases - and raises policy violations that designated reviewers can investigate and act on.

wrong.0: SharePoint Advanced Management governs site access and sharing.
wrong.2: Lifecycle management is about retention and deletion.
wrong.3: ID Protection scores sign-in and user risk.

questions.q: A Communication Compliance policy has flagged several messages. What is the reviewer's next step?
options: Delete the user's mailbox
Open the policy's pending alerts, examine the flagged messages in context, and resolve, escalate or tag them
Automatically report the user to law enforcement
Remove the user's Copilot licence
questions.explain: Flagged items land in a review queue. Reviewers see the message in context, then take an action such as resolving it, tagging it as compliant or non-compliant, notifying the user, or escalating for investigation.

wrong.0: Deletion destroys evidence and is not part of the workflow.
wrong.2: Escalation is an internal decision, not an automatic external report.
wrong.3: Licence removal is unrelated to a message review.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI?
options: To give a central view of AI activity and data risk, and to offer ready-made policies that protect data used by Copilot, agents and other AI apps
To build custom agents for departments
To replace conditional access for AI apps
To assign Copilot licences in bulk
questions.explain: DSPM for AI is the single pane for AI data security: it shows which AI apps people are using, what sensitive data appears in prompts and responses, runs data risk assessments for oversharing, and offers one-click policies to fix what it finds.

wrong.1: Agents are built in Copilot Studio, SharePoint or Agent Builder.
wrong.2: Conditional access still governs sign-in; DSPM for AI governs data.
wrong.3: Licences are handled in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

questions.q: Which AI applications can DSPM for AI report on?
options: Only Microsoft 365 Copilot
Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents, plus other AI apps such as ChatGPT and Gemini when devices are onboarded
Only Copilot Studio agents
Only third-party AI websites
questions.explain: DSPM for AI covers Microsoft AI experiences (Copilot, Copilot Chat, Copilot Studio, Security Copilot and more) and non-Microsoft AI apps. Seeing activity on third-party AI sites requires device onboarding to Purview and the Purview browser extension.

wrong.0: Its scope is deliberately wider than one product.
wrong.2: It is not limited to Copilot Studio.
wrong.3: Microsoft AI apps are its primary focus.

questions.q: Which DSPM for AI feature specifically helps find content that is overshared before Copilot is rolled out?
options: Conditional access what-if analysis
The Copilot usage report
Data risk assessments, which scan sites for potentially overshared items containing sensitive information
The message center
questions.explain: DSPM for AI runs a default weekly assessment on your busiest SharePoint sites and lets you build custom assessments. It shows which sites and items are broadly shared and contain sensitive data - the exact combination Copilot could surface.

wrong.0: That tests sign-in policies.
wrong.1: Usage reports show adoption numbers, not exposure.
wrong.3: The message center announces service changes.

questions.q: What is a sensitive information type (SIT) in Microsoft Purview?
options: A category of Entra ID security group
A type of Microsoft 365 licence
A permission level applied to a SharePoint site
A pattern definition, such as a credit card or passport number, used to detect specific data in content
questions.explain: A SIT is a detection pattern - regular expressions, keywords, checksums and confidence levels - that Purview uses to recognise things like credit card numbers, health identifiers or bank details inside documents and messages.

wrong.0: They have nothing to do with group types.
wrong.1: SITs are not licences.
wrong.2: Permission levels are a SharePoint concept.

questions.q: An organisation wants to detect documents that look like employment contracts, even though there is no fixed pattern to match. What should they use?
options: A conditional access policy
A trainable classifier, taught with sample documents
A retention label
A sensitive information type based on a regular expression
questions.explain: Trainable classifiers learn a category of content from examples rather than from a fixed pattern, which is what you need for document types such as contracts, resumes or source code where wording varies.

wrong.0: Conditional access governs access, not content type.
wrong.2: Retention labels decide how long to keep something.
wrong.3: Regex-based SITs work for structured patterns such as ID numbers, not for a document's overall nature.

questions.q: An administrator needs to see which files across the tenant contain sensitive information and where they are stored. Which tool shows this?
options: Activity explorer
The Entra ID audit log
Content explorer in Microsoft Purview data classification
The Teams admin center
questions.explain: Content explorer gives a current inventory: which sensitive information types and labels were found, and in which mailboxes, sites and accounts the items live. It answers 'what sensitive data do we have and where is it?'

wrong.0: Activity explorer shows what people did with labelled content, not the inventory.
wrong.1: Audit logs record actions, not content contents.
wrong.3: The Teams admin center manages Teams, not data classification.

cues: contain sensitive information and where they are stored

questions.q: Which tool shows actions taken on labelled content - such as label changes, downgrades and files copied to removable media?
options: Identity Secure Score
Content explorer
Compliance Manager
Activity explorer in Microsoft Purview
questions.explain: Activity explorer is the historical view: label applied, label changed, label removed, file copied, DLP rule matched, and AI interactions. It is where you go to see behaviour over time, including who downgraded a label.

wrong.0: Secure Score rates identity configuration.
wrong.1: Content explorer shows what exists right now, not the activity history.
wrong.2: Compliance Manager scores regulatory readiness.

questions.q: What are the two main outcomes a retention policy or label can enforce?
options: Assign a licence, and remove it
Encrypt content, and watermark it
Block sign-in, and require MFA
Retain content for a period, and delete it when the period expires
questions.explain: Retention answers two questions: keep it for how long, and what happens then. A policy can retain content so it cannot be permanently deleted during the period, delete it after the period, or do both in sequence.

wrong.0: That is licensing.
wrong.1: Encryption and marking come from sensitivity labels.
wrong.2: That is conditional access.

questions.q: What is the difference between a retention policy and a retention label?
options: A policy encrypts content; a label classifies it
A policy applies broadly to whole locations such as all SharePoint sites; a label is applied to individual items and can be user-applied or automatic
There is no difference
A policy is for email only; a label is for files only
questions.explain: Retention policies are container-level - point them at whole workloads or locations and everything inside inherits the setting. Retention labels are item-level, so a specific document or email gets its own retention treatment.

wrong.0: Neither performs encryption - that is Information Protection.
wrong.2: They differ in scope and in how they are applied.
wrong.3: Both can cover email and files.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes how Microsoft 365 Copilot decides what organisational content it can use?
options: It can use all content in the tenant regardless of permissions
It can only use content in the user's own OneDrive
It can only use content that has a sensitivity label
It can only use content the signed-in user already has at least view permission to
questions.explain: Copilot enforces the existing Microsoft 365 permission model on every request. Grounding is done in the context of the signed-in user, so nothing appears in an answer that the person could not have opened themselves.

wrong.0: Copilot never bypasses permissions.
wrong.1: It draws on everything the user can reach - mail, chats, Teams, SharePoint - not just OneDrive.
wrong.2: Labels affect protection, not whether content can be used at all.

questions.q: What role does Microsoft Graph play in Copilot responses?
options: It is the billing system for Copilot licences
It stores the large language model used by Copilot
It encrypts Copilot prompts before they leave the device
It provides the work context - emails, chats, meetings, files and people - that Copilot uses to ground its answers in your organisation's data
questions.explain: Microsoft Graph is the connective layer holding your organisation's content and relationships. Copilot retrieves relevant material from Graph, adds it to the prompt, and the model answers using that grounded context instead of guessing.

wrong.0: Billing lives in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
wrong.1: The models are hosted in the Azure OpenAI service within Microsoft's service boundary.
wrong.2: Encryption is handled by the service, not by Graph.

questions.q: What does the semantic index add to Microsoft 365 Copilot?
options: A representation of content and its meaning that improves how relevant material is found, while still respecting each user's permissions
A backup copy of all tenant data outside the service boundary
A queue of Copilot prompts waiting to be billed
A public search index shared with other tenants
questions.explain: The semantic index lets Copilot find content by meaning rather than only by exact keywords, so answers are grounded in more relevant material. Crucially, it enforces the same identity-based access boundaries as the rest of Microsoft 365.

wrong.1: Nothing leaves the Microsoft 365 service boundary for this.
wrong.2: Indexing is unrelated to billing.
wrong.3: Tenant data is never shared across tenants.

questions.q: Are Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph used to train the foundation large language models?
options: Only prompts from trial tenants are used
Only if the user opts in during first use
Yes - all prompts are used to improve the models
No - they are not used to train the foundation models
questions.explain: Microsoft states plainly that prompts, responses and Graph-accessed data are not used to train the foundation LLMs. This is one of the core commitments behind enterprise data protection for Copilot.

wrong.0: There is no trial-tenant exception for foundation model training.
wrong.1: It is not an opt-in behaviour.
wrong.2: This is the misconception the commitment exists to correct.

questions.q: Where are a user's Copilot prompts and responses stored, and how can they be managed?
options: They are discarded immediately and cannot be reviewed
On the user's local device only
In the user's Copilot activity history inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary, discoverable via Purview and deletable by the user
In a shared public repository
questions.explain: Interactions are kept as Copilot activity history within the service boundary. Users can delete their own history from the My Account portal, and admins can search, retain or apply eDiscovery to it through Microsoft Purview.

wrong.0: They are retained and are discoverable for compliance.
wrong.1: Storage is in the service, not just on the device.
wrong.3: Tenant data is never placed in a public repository.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists Microsoft's responsible AI principles?
options: Speed; accuracy; cost; scale; uptime; support
Detect; protect; respond; recover
Verify explicitly; least privilege; assume breach
Fairness; reliability and safety; privacy and security; inclusiveness; transparency; accountability
questions.explain: Microsoft's six responsible AI principles are fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability - with transparency and accountability underpinning the other four.

wrong.0: These are service quality attributes, not AI principles.
wrong.1: That resembles a cybersecurity framework lifecycle.
wrong.2: Those are the Zero Trust principles.

questions.q: An organisation tells staff clearly when they are interacting with an AI agent and explains what data it uses. Which responsible AI principle is being applied?
options: Fairness
Inclusiveness
Reliability and safety
Transparency
questions.explain: Transparency means people can understand how an AI system works and when it is being used, so they can judge its output sensibly. Telling users they are talking to an agent is a textbook example.

wrong.0: Fairness is about avoiding biased outcomes across groups.
wrong.1: Inclusiveness is about designing for people of all abilities and backgrounds.
wrong.2: Reliability and safety is about consistent, safe behaviour under expected conditions.

questions.q: What does Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager provide?
options: A real-time feed of blocked sign-ins
The ability to create custom agents
An inventory of every file in SharePoint
A compliance score with improvement actions mapped to regulations and standards such as GDPR and ISO 27001
questions.explain: Compliance Manager assesses your tenant against regulatory templates, gives you a compliance score, and lists improvement actions with the technical steps and the evidence you need for an audit.

wrong.0: Sign-in data lives in Entra logs.
wrong.1: Agents are built in Copilot Studio or Agent Builder.
wrong.2: File inventory comes from content explorer or SharePoint reports.

questions.q: A legal team needs to find every email and document mentioning a specific project across the tenant. Which tool should be used?
options: Activity explorer
Entra sign-in logs
Copilot Analytics
Content search in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery
questions.explain: Content search in eDiscovery queries mailboxes, SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts and Teams content with keywords and conditions, then lets you preview and export the results for a legal or investigative case.

wrong.0: Activity explorer shows actions on labelled content, not full-text search of everything.
wrong.1: Sign-in logs record authentication only.
wrong.2: Copilot Analytics reports on Copilot adoption.

questions.q: Why is it important that Copilot interactions are discoverable through eDiscovery?
options: So agents can reuse other people's prompts
Prompts and responses are business records that may be required for legal holds, investigations and regulatory requests
So users can be billed for each prompt
So Microsoft can improve the model
questions.explain: Copilot conversations are treated like any other Microsoft 365 content: they can be searched, placed on hold, retained and exported, which is what regulators and legal teams expect of workplace communication.

wrong.0: Prompts are not shared between users this way.
wrong.2: eDiscovery is unrelated to billing.
wrong.3: Discoverability is a customer compliance feature, not model improvement.

questions.q: What is 'oversharing' in the context of a Copilot deployment?
options: Too many licences were purchased
Users send too many Copilot prompts per day
Agents are shared with too many departments
Content is accessible to far more people than intended, so Copilot can surface it in answers to users who should not see it
questions.explain: Oversharing means permissions are broader than the business intended - a site shared with 'Everyone except external users', a link sent to the whole company. Copilot does not create the problem, but it makes the consequences visible immediately.

wrong.0: Licence count has nothing to do with content exposure.
wrong.1: That is a usage or cost question.
wrong.2: Agent distribution is separate from content permissions.

questions.q: Which SharePoint report identifies the sites most broadly shared using 'Everyone except external users'?
options: Identity Secure Score
The Teams usage report
The Copilot licence assignment report
A data access governance report in the SharePoint admin center
questions.explain: Data access governance (DAG) reports in the SharePoint admin center highlight exposure: sites shared with 'Everyone except external users', sites with the most sharing links, and permission baselines - so you can fix the worst offenders before enabling Copilot.

wrong.0: Secure Score rates identity configuration.
wrong.1: That measures Teams adoption.
wrong.2: Licence reports show assignment, not sharing.

questions.q: Which SharePoint Advanced Management feature restricts access to a site so that only members of a specified Microsoft Entra security group or Microsoft 365 group can open it, regardless of previously granted permissions?
options: Site lifecycle management
Restricted access control
Microsoft 365 Archive
Restricted content discovery
questions.explain: Restricted access control puts a hard boundary around a site: only members of the nominated group can get in, even if someone else was granted permission earlier or holds a sharing link. It is the strongest containment option for a sensitive site.

wrong.0: Lifecycle management handles ownership, inactivity and attestation.
wrong.2: Archive moves inactive sites to a cheaper storage tier.
wrong.3: Restricted content discovery hides a site from Copilot and org-wide search but leaves permissions working.

questions.q: A site must stay usable for its team, but should never appear in Microsoft 365 Copilot answers or organisation-wide search. Which feature fits best?
options: A DLP policy
Restricted access control
Restricted content discovery
A retention policy
questions.explain: Restricted content discovery excludes a site from Copilot and tenant-wide search results while leaving existing permissions untouched, so the team keeps working normally and the content simply stops surfacing elsewhere.

wrong.0: DLP governs sharing of sensitive data, not search visibility.
wrong.1: That would cut off users who currently need the site.
wrong.3: Retention affects how long content is kept.

questions.q: What does a site access review in SharePoint Advanced Management do?
options: Asks site owners to confirm or remove the access shown in a governance report
Encrypts every document in the site
Assigns Copilot licences to site owners
Automatically deletes all guest accounts
questions.explain: Site access reviews push the decision to the people who actually know: the admin flags sites from a DAG report, and owners review who has access and remove what is no longer appropriate. It scales oversharing cleanup beyond the IT team.

wrong.1: Encryption comes from sensitivity labels.
wrong.2: Licensing is unrelated.
wrong.3: Nothing is deleted automatically.

questions.q: Which combination best describes a practical approach to reducing oversharing before enabling Copilot?
options: Turn off SharePoint search for all users
Run data access governance reports, apply sensitivity labels and DLP, use restricted access control on sensitive sites, and run access reviews
Disable multifactor authentication to simplify troubleshooting
Give every user Read access to every site so nothing looks unusual
questions.explain: Oversharing is fixed in layers: find the exposure with reports and DSPM for AI assessments, classify and protect the sensitive material with labels and DLP, contain the worst sites with restricted access control or restricted content discovery, and keep it clean with reviews.

wrong.0: Disabling search cripples productivity without fixing permissions.
wrong.2: Weakening authentication is never a governance improvement.
wrong.3: That makes oversharing dramatically worse.

questions.q: How do Microsoft 365 permissions, Purview and Defender work together to protect Copilot?
options: Defender assigns Copilot licences
Permissions decide what content can be reached, Purview classifies and governs it, and Defender protects against threats and risky activity
Each product must be configured separately for every prompt
Purview replaces Microsoft 365 permissions for Copilot
questions.explain: They are layers of the same defence. Access control determines reachable content, Purview adds classification, labels, DLP and lifecycle rules on top, and Defender guards against the threats and attacks that could abuse the whole setup.

wrong.0: Defender does no licensing.
wrong.2: Policies are configured once and applied continuously, not per prompt.
wrong.3: Purview builds on permissions; it does not replace them.

questions.q: An organisation must keep finance records for seven years and then delete them automatically. Which Purview solution handles this?
options: Microsoft Defender XDR
Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance
questions.explain: Data Lifecycle Management is where retention policies and labels live - defining how long content is kept, what triggers the clock, and whether it is deleted or reviewed at the end of the period.

wrong.0: Defender XDR handles threat protection.
wrong.2: Insider Risk Management detects risky user behaviour.
wrong.3: Communication Compliance reviews message content for policy violations.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Microsoft 365 Copilot and an agent?
options: Agents are only available to administrators
Agents replace Copilot once they are published
Copilot is the broad assistant across Microsoft 365 apps; an agent is scoped to specific instructions, knowledge and actions for a defined task
Copilot works offline while agents require internet access
questions.explain: Copilot is the general assistant grounded in your whole work context. An agent is purpose-built: you give it instructions, a limited set of knowledge sources, and sometimes actions, so it behaves consistently for one job such as answering HR policy questions.

wrong.0: Agents are built and used by ordinary users too, subject to admin policy.
wrong.1: Agents extend Copilot; they do not replace it.
wrong.3: Both are cloud services and need connectivity.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a declarative agent from a custom engine agent?
options: A declarative agent must be written in C#; a custom engine agent uses no code
A declarative agent uses Copilot's existing model and orchestration with your instructions and knowledge; a custom engine agent brings its own model and orchestration logic
There is no difference - the terms are interchangeable
A declarative agent runs only in Excel; a custom engine agent runs only in Teams
questions.explain: Declarative agents are configuration on top of Copilot: instructions, knowledge sources, and optionally actions. Custom engine agents supply their own model and orchestration, which makes them more flexible and more suited to autonomous behaviour.

wrong.0: Declarative agents are typically built with no code in Agent Builder, SharePoint or Copilot Studio.
wrong.2: They differ substantially in architecture and capability.
wrong.3: Neither type is limited to a single app.

questions.q: A business user with no coding skills wants to create an agent that answers questions from the documents in one SharePoint site. What is the simplest option?

Create a SharePoint agent on that site, or build a declarative agent in Agent Builder
Deploy an Azure virtual machine to host the agent
Write a custom engine agent using the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
questions.explain: SharePoint agents are made in a couple of clicks from a site or document library and are grounded in that content. Agent Builder inside Copilot is the other no-code route for a declarative agent.

wrong.0: Support tickets are for problems, not agent creation.
wrong.2: No infrastructure is needed - this is a SaaS capability.
wrong.3: The Agents Toolkit is a developer tool requiring code.

questions.q: Which tool is designed for makers to build more advanced agents with custom topics, actions, connectors and autonomous triggers?
options: The SharePoint recycle bin
The Exchange admin center
Microsoft Copilot Studio
Microsoft Purview
questions.explain: Copilot Studio is the low-code maker environment for agents: knowledge sources, topics, actions, connectors, triggers and publishing channels, with governance surfaced in the Power Platform admin center.

wrong.0: That is not a tool at all.
wrong.1: Exchange administers mailboxes and mail flow.
wrong.3: Purview handles compliance and data governance.
